Summoned entities

  •  Manifestation of Tyranny – Gortash summons a fixed number of these creatures into specific places in the room. These have no place in the initiative order but each one applies 1 stack of the aura condition  Bane's Brutality to Gortash and nearby Black Gauntlet characters, as long as they are standing within a short distance.
  • Bane's Fist – After Gortash summons it, it is inserted into the end of the turn order. At the end of each of its turns, Bane's Fist punches the ground around it for a lot of damage.

Conditions

This information is not specified on this character's Examine page, but has resulted from contributor testing. If this information varies depending on whether this character is hostile, allied, or neutral, then please specify this in the applicable section.

Unique

Gortash has access to the following unique conditions, but is not necessarily the caster of these conditions.

  •  Avatar of Tyranny
  •  Bane's Brutality

Temporary

Gortash can gain certain defensive buffs or debuffs from his Reflectoguards and nearby traps:

  •  Malfunctioning Shell of Resistance (from Deranged Force Curtain)
  •  Reflectoguard Active (from a thrown Reflectoguard)
  •  Shell of Resistance (from Micromodron Force Curtain)

Encounter details

Wyrm's Rock Fortress (Audience Hall)

If the party attack Gortash during his coronation ceremony, one of the most difficult fights in all of Baldur's Gate 3 begins. Gortash is accompanied by  Ulder Ravengard, an army of  Steel Watchers and Flaming Fists, and numerous traps along the walls.

Gortash begins combat with  Shell of Resistance cast on him by a nearby force curtain, and throws  Reflectoguards at himself and  Phase Optimizers at nearby Steel Watchers. This gives him immunity or resistance to most types of damage and make him very difficult to kill quickly, while turning all Steel Watchers into even more dangerous threats.

Gortash has +5 Initiative (+10 on Tactician and Honour modes) and all Steel Watchers have +6 Initiative, making them very likely to act early in the turn order. Considering that there are 9 Steel Watchers in addition to Gortash, it is easily possible for an unprepared party to be killed in a single turn.

The traps along the walls can also be quite dangerous. Grenade Impellers and Incineration Casters fire projectiles that constantly force the party to move, while Micromodron Force Curtains repeatedly grant Gortash many resistances and immunities. However the Deranged Force Curtains are malfunctioning and can debuff Gortash with  Malfunctioning Shell of Resistance to reduce his defenses.

Once per fight, when damaged to 75% HP or below, Gortash can cast  Invoke the Black Hand, giving him 150 temporary hit points,  Advantage on Strength checks and saving throws, an extra 1d4⁠⁠Physical damage to unarmed attacks, and immunity to ⁠Thunder, ⁠Fire, and ⁠Force damage. He also gains the ability to use  Tyrant's Bindings,  Empowered Unarmed Strike, and  The Closed Fist of Bane. This makes him significantly more durable and drastically increases his damage.

Wyrm's Rock Fortress (Gortash's Office)

If the party does not fight him at his coronation, they can return to Gortash in his office later on. After agreeing to his deal during ⁠Consider Gortash's Bargain and finishing ⁠Get Orin's Netherstone, the party can attempt to fulfill the bargain. If the party destroys the Steel Watch Foundry or travels to the Iron Throne, he becomes hostile and begins combat on sight.

If the party return to the lower floors of Wyrm's Rock after destroying the Steel Watch Foundry, the Flaming Fists are already hostile, and the party must fight their way up through the Audience Hall and its traps and guards in order to reach Gortash's office on the top floor. This sometimes results in a bug.[See: Bugs]

Gortash's high initiative, conditional buffs from traps and Reflectoguards, and his spells and features remain the same.

In the statue hall leading to Gortash's office, and in his office itself, several traps, such as Grenade Impellers, Incineration Casters. Micromodron Force Curtains and Deranged Force Curtains can be found placed along the walls.

Morphic Pool

If the party allied with Gortash, but then strike him twice during ⁠Confront the Elder Brain, despite his warning the first time, Gortash gets furious at the player character's blatant disrespect and turns hostile.

Out of all three scenarios, this battle is the easiest. Not only are there no traps for the party to watch out for, Gortash has no Steel Watchers or Banites to guard him.

Gortash's high initiative, Reflectoguards, and his spells and features remain the same.

Tactics

Wyrm's Rock Fortress (Audience Hall)

This fight is immensely difficult and requires immaculate planning since the action economy is so stacked against the party.

The high initiative and area of effect attacks of the Steel Watchers threaten to end the fight before it even fully begins. This practically necessitates that the party increase their initiative as well. This can be done through the  Alert feat, an  Elixir of Vigilance, or equipment which increases initiative (see Initiative bonuses).

The party can take advantage of the Steel Watcher's  Self-Detonate ability by luring them into the close proximity of other enemies and allowing them to blow each other up.

The Micromodron Force Curtains make it very difficult to damage Gortash for as long as they're intact. Destroying them while leaving malfunctioning Deranged Force Curtains intact reduces his resistances and makes it easier to defeat him.

Wyrm's Rock Fortress (Gortash's Office)

This fight is significantly easier than the coronation fight, especially if ⁠Disable the Steel Watch is completed to take out the Steel Watchers. All advice from the previous section also applies here.

Gortash's Black Gauntlet allies can be dangerous due to their  Command and  Dominate Person spells. They should be taken out quickly before they get a chance to use them.

While the lower floors of the fortress are already hostile if the Steel Watch Foundry is destroyed, they can be bypassed entirely by using  Grant Flight,  Feather Fall, or  Misty Step to jump from Wyrm's Crossing to the rocky area around the base of the fortress. The party can then safely ascend the vines on the western side of the building and jump up the platforms on the southwestern rampart.

A very effective strategy to defeat Gortash and his allies is to lure them out of his office and into the foyer outside, thereby avoiding all traps. This is done most effectively by sending one party member to initiate combat with Gortash, and then moving the party member very quickly through either dashing or teleporting (e.g.  Dimension Door) back towards the door outside. Placing spells like  Hunger of Hadar,  Insect Plague, and  Cloudkill around the door and shoving enemies back into it trivialises the encounter as Gortash and his allies constantly take massive damage trying to pursue the party through the door.

Finally, as with many other encounters where combat is not immediately imposed on the party, Gortash and his entourage on the top floor can be easily defeated by stealthy means. Although this is a more tedious method, it is a safe and reliable path to victory, and may therefore be preferable in Honour mode; refer to this guide for more details. If using stealthy means, the chosen party member must deal with the first  Steel Watcher after reaching the top floor. Here, one can use the  Titanstring Bow in conjunction with an  Elixir of Cloud Giant Strength with excellent odds of sneak attacking it from a distance while successfully maintaining  Greater Invisibility until it explodes. If using this tactic in Honour mode, it is advisable to recast  Greater Invisibility as needed to ensure the exponentially increasing Stealth check difficulty from repeated attacks does not break the spell. Once the first Steel Watcher is destroyed, normal stealth attacks without invisibility can be used to slowly remove opponents outside of Gortash's Office proper.

To finish Gortash sooner with stealth tactics, before he uses  Invoke the Black Hand, once he is reduced below 75% of his full hit points, it is advisable to use scrolls of  Greater Invisibility as needed while placing about 10  Smokepowder Bombs next to him. Then move to a safe distance and throw one more at him to finish him off; his remaining guards are a trivial matter.

Bugs

  • Fighting in the Audience Hall after destroying the Steel Watch Foundry can sometimes trigger the enemies on the top floor to become involved in the combat. In this case Gortash and his allies may make an appearance near the entrance to the Audience Hall (despite this not being the door to the location they are coming from). This can make the fight easier as Gortash is further from his most deadly traps, but can also make the fight difficult by adding an unexpected wave of additional enemies.
  • Gortash can repeatedly Invoke the Black Hand after having a condition applied to him while at 75% HP or below. This occurs after he has activated Avatar of Tyranny. Once this bug appears, the only solution is to deal enough damage in a single attack (not turn) to kill him, which must be at least over 150 damage. If fighting in Gortash's office, it is possible to defeat him by pushing him off the balcony to the east of the office, after which his body can be found on the beach below.
  • Due to a bug related to a hidden passive that unlocks Invoke the Black Hand for Gortash, he is immune to  Slimy Doom: Stunned and never becomes  Stunned when  Stricken With Slimy Doom. The remaining  Contagion conditions appear to be unaffected.
